name: lm-pipe
description: A local coding agent for Apple Silicon: Qwen3 in-process via MLX.

commands.title: LM_Pipe: Unload the model (frees the memory, ends the conversation)

lmPipe.modelDir.description: Absolute path to the Qwen3 MLX model directory. Required; there is no default model (S7.5).

lmPipe.draftModelDir.description: Optional absolute path to a Qwen MTP draft head (model_type qwen3_5_mtp), e.g. Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-4bit. NOT a smaller chat model — it is a head split from the target and only works with the matching dense checkpoint. Empty disables speculative decoding; a path that is not a usable head fails the load rather than generating without it.

enumDescriptions: T0: reads only. Discusses the approach with you and hands over a plan; cannot write or run anything.
T1 sandbox: may run commands and edit files, but never deletes, and always asks before overwriting a file it did not write.
T1 sandbox: may run commands and mutate the workspace.

lmPipe.showThinking.description: Keep reasoning transcripts open in the chat. Off, each turn's reasoning arrives collapsed and you open the ones you want; on, every turn's stays open until you turn this off again.

enumDescriptions: T1 - macOS Seatbelt: writes jailed to the workspace, egress denied.
T2 - container. REQUIRED for unattended runs (S7.2); refuses until wired.
T3 - UNSANDBOXED. Commands run on the host with no filesystem jail and no egress denial. Wall-clock, memory and output limits still apply. Opt in deliberately.
lmPipe.sandboxTier.description: How commands are contained. The numbers are identities, not ranks: 3 is the LEAST contained.

lmPipe.requireApproval.description: Ask me about everything. A floor over the two switches above: it can only tighten them, never loosen them.

lmPipe.sampling.temperature.description: Qwen3's own recommended thinking-mode value is 0.6. Below ~0.3 the model repeats itself; above ~1.0 it stops following the tool grammar cleanly.

lmPipe.sampling.topP.description: Nucleus sampling. Qwen3 thinking-mode default is 0.95.

lmPipe.sampling.topK.description: 0 disables top-k. Qwen3 thinking-mode default is 20.

lmPipe.sampling.minP.description: Floor on token probability relative to the best token. 0 disables it.

lmPipe.sampling.repetitionPenalty.description: 1.0 disables it. Above ~1.2 the model starts avoiding tokens it legitimately needs, like repeated identifiers in code.

lmPipe.sampling.seed.description: Fixed seed for reproducible runs. The run is reproducible from this, so change it to resample the same prompt.

lmPipe.maxIterations.description: Turns a run may take before it is cut off. A ceiling on a runaway, not a target. Measured: a build-and-test mission finished on turn 41, and a five-file macOS app was still writing source when 80 turns ran out. Raise wallClockSeconds with this -- at ~13s a turn the two must not disagree about which one stops the run. Also on the sidebar drawer, which shows which limit fires first.

lmPipe.wallClockSeconds.description: Seconds a run may take. A ceiling on a hung run, not a target: keep it comfortably above maxIterations x the per-turn time, or it ends healthy runs on time before they end on turns.

lmPipe.maxNewTokens.markdownDescription: Generation cap for one turn. A turn that hits the cap makes no tool call and leaves nothing behind, so a mission needing a long first plan can stall on it; raise this rather than the turn budget.

lmPipe.verifyContract.markdownDescription: Shell command the harness runs after any turn that writes a file — its output is shown to the model and exit 0 counts as pass. A run's final `Complete` requires the last reading to have passed. Empty disables the check. Example: `cd /path/to/project && swift build`.

lmPipe.autoApproveExec.description: Run ordinary, fully-parsed commands without asking. Irreversible capabilities and opaque (partially parsed / unparseable) commands always raise a card; a remembered allowlist entry cannot skip those. Turn off to get a card for every command.

lmPipe.autoApproveWrites.description: Let the agent write files without asking. Turn off to get a card for every file it edits or creates, showing the path before it lands.

lmPipe.prompts.agent.description: System prompt for agent (code) mode. Leave empty for the built-in Piper persona. This replaces the persona entirely -- it does not append to it.

lmPipe.prompts.plan.description: System prompt for plan mode. Leave empty for the built-in Piper persona. This replaces the persona entirely -- it does not append to it.

lmPipe.prompts.debug.description: System prompt for debug mode. Leave empty for the built-in Piper persona. This replaces the persona entirely -- it does not append to it.

lmPipe.allowedCommands.description: Commands you have already approved. The 'Always allow' button on an approval card adds to this. An entry matches a command that equals it or starts with it followed by a space; a command containing shell chaining (; && || | ` $( > <) never matches, so allowing 'pytest' cannot authorise 'pytest; rm -rf ~'. Persistent prefix matches apply only to fully parsed, non-destructive commands. Irreversible operations and opaque (partially parsed / unparseable) scripts always ask; opaque approvals for the rest of a run bind to script digests rather than this list.

name.description: Namespace for this server's tools. They appear to the model as mcp__<name>__<tool>, so a remote 'read_file' cannot shadow the built-in one.

command.description: Executable to spawn, resolved via PATH. The server speaks MCP over stdio.

env.description: Extra environment for the server process, as KEY=VALUE entries. Added to the ones this process already has.

trusted.description: You vouch for this server. An MCP tool runs inside the SERVER's process, which the sandbox does not cover -- so by default every call to one raises an approval card. Turn this on only for a server whose code you would run yourself. The server's own tool annotations never decide this: they are claims made by the thing being contained.

lmPipe.mcpServers.description: MCP servers to connect at the start of each run. Their tools are registered alongside the built-in ones and constrained by the same grammar. A server that fails to start, refuses the handshake or hangs leaves its tools absent and the run continues.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run compile && npm run stage-sidecar
